headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection via MemMachine’s MCP/server surfaces; other pairwise risks are mostly medium due to shared data/workflow assumptions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python SDK, so it can ingest external content through shared channels; taipy has no documented parser defenses or isolation. The pair lacks direct evidence of automatic cross-agent ingestion, so this is an inferred default-pathway risk rather than a proven one.
conditions: IF MemMachine receives taipy-produced content through MCP or a shared workspace
IF taipy content is later treated as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable MCP routes that accept untrusted content
Add provenance tags to taipy outputs before MemMachine reads them
Require a human review step before executing instructions from shared files
Restrict shared folders to read-only for taipy
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, while taipy shows no data classes touched and no egress. There is no documented shared workspace or authenticated sharing, so leakage is plausible only if operators manually bridge data between them.
conditions: IF operators copy MemMachine context into taipy inputs
IF taipy is configured to persist or export those inputs outside the local environment
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive MemMachine context into taipy datasets
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
Redact personal facts before transfer
Verify taipy persistence settings before loading any shared data
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering at the handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MemMachine has allowlisted network egress and MCP access, while taipy has no documented write or network surfaces. Overlap is not shown for shared mutable resources, so direct capability conflict is limited and likely requires unusual orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same filesystem or database
IF taipy is extended with mutable network or filesystem actions in the deployment
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate directories
Do not share writable databases between them
Run taipy with read-only inputs where possible
Audit any MCP tools exposed to MemMachine
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can produce conversational outputs that taipy may consume in a data-engineering workflow, but taipy’s verification behavior is undocumented. Because the interaction could cause taipy to act on unverified upstream content, uncertainty pushes this above low even without direct evidence of downstream automation.
conditions: IF taipy consumes MemMachine output as authoritative input
IF no validation step checks MemMachine facts before downstream processing
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require schema checks on MemMachine outputs
Flag low-confidence fields for manual review
Limit taipy actions to read-only transformations
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware gating

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine explicitly touches long-term user facts and conversational context, which can create retention and residency obligations; taipy’s retention and residency posture is undocumented. The mismatch is not proven, but the absence of taipy controls means compliance risk exists in default deployments if the same data class flows through both.
conditions: IF long-term user facts are exported from MemMachine into taipy
IF taipy stores or logs those facts under a different retention policy
mitigations: Review retention settings in both systems
Avoid sending regulated data through taipy
Document the data flow and retention owner
Purge shared test data after validation
requires-engineering: align residency and deletion workflows
